note:
R67 - PS4 EA-MP3 (SNS codec 0x0b, NHL 15-17 speech): parse each data block as a chain of SIZED frames and test the reading on all
r61 vectors (read-only over the banks; temporary .mp3/.wav in the scratchpad, removed unless --keep).

Grammar under test (from the r61 prefix values, which read as little-endian u16 = MPEG frame bytes + 2):
    ea_frame := u16le hdr ; [ u32le pcm_samples ; ] mpeg_frame ; [ pcm_samples x s16le ]
        size  = hdr & 0x7fff          total bytes of the ea_frame including the u16
        flag  = hdr & 0x8000          when set, a u32le PCM sample count follows and that many s16le samples trail the MPEG frame
    block payload := ea_frame+        (no padding; the sizes must tile the payload exactly)
Every MPEG frame keeps its own 4-byte header (so nothing was "removed"); frames may use the bit reservoir (main_data_begin) - the side
info is parsed so that is measured, not assumed. Decoding is done twice with independent implementations inside ffmpeg (`mp3` fixed-point
and `mp3float`) on the concatenated MPEG frames; the declared SNR num_samples, the WAV sample counts, channel and rate, and the embedded
PCM are all compared. Nothing is written back; no encoder is claimed.
Usage: python r67_ea_mp3_sized_frames.py <out.json> [--titles nhl15,nhl16,nhl17] [--per-title 8] [--keep]
